title: A student's isotherm map
body: A student is given a base map showing the point locations of five weather stations with their mean July temperatures: 22, 27, 31, 36 and 41 degrees Celsius. She finds the minimum and maximum values, uses interpolation to locate points between neighbouring stations, and draws smooth isotherms with a French curve, beginning with the lowest value. She chooses to draw the isotherms of 23, 29, 34 and 40 degrees Celsius and writes each value along its line by breaking the line in the middle. Her teacher returns the map, saying that one rule for drawing isopleths has not been followed.
